title: The Dictionary With No Words In It
subtitle: 语言文化 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 语言文化（历史社会与文化·语言与文化）
meta: 主题语境：语言文化（历史社会与文化·语言与文化）　|　核心词汇：hand　|　正文 347 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 hand 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: My grandmother spoke three languages and wrote none of them, which is why I spent eleven summers sitting beside her with a pencil. Her ① hand was small and very fast, and she could not read it back; she wrote for the ear, not the eye. What she wrote, I later understood, was a dictionary with no definitions in it — a ② hand reaching across forty years to somebody who had not been born.

She had one rule. I was to write exactly what she said and correct nothing, because on the other ③ hand a corrected sentence is a different sentence, and usually a worse one. When I broke the rule at twelve, she took the pencil from me and ④ handed it back only when I had promised to change nothing again.

A corrected page, she said, is a page with somebody else's hand in it. There were ⑤ hands involved beyond ours. A cousin in Marseille typed the French pages, a woman at the church ⑥ handed out the Arabic ones to anybody who would read them, and a retired teacher corrected the spelling of a language none of us spoke. At ⑦ hand, always, was the problem that my grandmother did not care about spelling, and the teacher did not care about anything else.

In 2009 the notebooks were given to a university, and I learned ⑧ at first hand what an archive does to a voice: a hand wrote a catalogue entry describing them as 'informal correspondence'. That is accurate and useless. On the one ⑨ hand they are letters between relatives; on the other they are the only record of a dialect that has since gone quiet, and the dialect is the part that matters.

I have the pencil. Her writing, I can now see, was not careless; it was a ⑩ hand made for speed, shaped by a life of kitchens and markets where nothing was written down twice. What I learned from her is the thing I still teach: a language is not a set of rules that somebody hands you. It is something you have to take.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 笔迹；字迹（a hand）
C. n. （参与做事的）人手；帮手；方面
D. v. 递；交给（hand sb sth）
E. 固定搭配：on the one hand ..., on the other (hand) 一方面……另一方面
F. 固定搭配：at hand 在手边；即将发生／摆在面前
G. 固定搭配：hand out 分发；散发
H. 固定搭配：at first hand 直接地；亲身地

items.q: Her hand was small and very fast
a hand reaching across forty years
because on the other hand a corrected sentence
handed it back only when I had promised
There were hands involved beyond ours
At hand, always, was the problem
I learned at first hand what an archive does to a voice
On the one hand they are letters between relatives
it was a hand made for speed

answers.why: 此处 hand 指“笔迹、字迹”，说她的字小而快，自己都认不回。
指“手”，比喻跨越四十年伸向未来的一只手。
on the other hand 意为“另一方面”，此处说改过的句子就成了另一句。
hand 作动词，意为“递、交还”，说她把笔递回给我，直到我答应不再改动。
hands 指参与的“人手、方面”，除我们之外还有别人参与。
hand out 意为“分发”，说教堂那位女士把阿拉伯语页分给大家读。
at hand 意为“摆在面前、近在手边”，说这个问题始终存在。
at first hand 意为“亲身地、直接地”，说我亲眼看到档案馆如何处置一个人的声音。
On the one hand ... on the other 意为“一方面……另一方面”，与第 3 题同组搭配。
再次指“笔迹”，说那是一种为求快而形成的写法。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 她的字小而快，自己都认不回来。（hand）
另一方面，改过的句子就成了另一句。（on the other hand）
除了我们，还有别的人手参与其中。（hands）
教堂那位女士把阿拉伯语的那些页分给愿意读的人。（hand out）
这个问题始终摆在眼前。（at hand）
一方面它们是家书，另一方面它们是一种方言的唯一记录。（on the one hand）
answers: Her hand was small and very fast, and she could not read it back.
On the other hand, a corrected sentence is a different sentence.
There were hands involved beyond ours.
The woman at the church handed out the Arabic pages to anybody who would read them.
The problem was always at hand.
On the one hand they are letters between relatives; on the other they are the only record of a dialect.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 hand 的 3 种不同用法；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: Her hand was small and very fast, and she could not read it back.
She took the pencil from my hand and wrote the sentence again herself, the wrong way.
There were hands involved beyond ours: a cousin in Marseille and a woman at the church.
The woman at the church handed out the Arabic pages, and the problem of spelling was always at hand.
On the one hand the notebooks are letters between relatives; on the other they are the only record of a dialect.
Her hand, I can now see, was made for speed, shaped by a life of kitchens and markets.
